label: prf:bar-t-duality-substrate
title: Proof of bar t duality substrate
html:
Proof. Proof of bar t duality substrate

Proof. The substitution q \mapsto q^{-1} in the Weierstrass coefficients p(q) and r(q) yields rational functions p^*(q) = p(q^{-1}) and r^*(q) = r(q^{-1}), defining the curve \mathcal{E}_{q^{-1}} : y^2 = x^3 + p^*(q)\,x + r^*(q). The map \iota_* \colon \mathcal{E}_q \to \mathcal{E}_{q^{-1}} is defined by (x, y, q) \mapsto (x, y, q^{-1}) on the total space \mathcal{X} = \{(x, y, q) : y^2 = x^3 + p(q)x + r(q)\} and is an involution since \iota \circ \iota = \mathrm{id}.

(1) The condition \Delta(\mathcal{E}_q) = -4p(q)^3 - 27r(q)^2 = 0 at q = 1/\varphi^2 implies \Delta(\mathcal{E}_{1/q}) = -4p(1/q)^3 - 27r(1/q)^2 = 0 at 1/q = 1/\varphi^2, meaning q = \varphi^2.

(2) The j-invariant j(\mathcal{E}_q) = -1728 \cdot 64\,p(q)^3 / \Delta(q) pulls back along \iota to j^*(q) := j(\mathcal{E}_{1/q}) = j(q^{-1}), a well-defined rational function of q.

(3) By bar-self-dual confinement band, the open interval \mathcal{B} = (1/\varphi^2, \varphi^2) is the maximal \iota-invariant open subset of \mathbb{R}_{>0} avoiding the golden nodes. This makes it the maximal locus where both \mathcal{E}_q and \mathcal{E}_{1/q} are simultaneously non-degenerate. \square

This property implies that any statement of the form "\mathcal{E}_q has property P for q \in I \subset \mathcal{B}" automatically yields its bar conjugate: "\mathcal{E}_{1/q} has property P for q \in \iota(I)." We extend proofs about the elliptic family from the sub-classical wing (1/\varphi^2,\,1) to the super-classical wing (1,\,\varphi^2) by composing with \iota_*. Thus, a deconfinement statement such as "q < 1/\varphi^2 \Rightarrow deconfined" yields the bar companion "q > \varphi^2 \Rightarrow deconfined" directly.

Substrate-level bar T-duality is the geometric shadow of the Iwahori–Hecke bar involution \overline{\,\cdot\,} \colon H_n(q) \to H_n(q^{-1}) given by \sigma_i \mapsto \sigma_i^{-1}. Because the Descartes elliptic curve \mathcal{E}_q arises from the Markov trace (Descartes elliptic curve), the Hecke bar involution descends to \iota on the moduli parameter.
